name: AI law and regulation effective dates by jurisdiction
description: When each AI-specific law, regulation and milestone actually takes effect — the instrument, the provision that states the date, the date itself, what it applies to, and the statutory text quoted verbatim from the enacted bill or the official journal. Answers 'when does the Colorado AI Act take effect', 'when do the EU AI Act high-risk obligations apply', 'when does Texas HB 149 start', 'what date does the Illinois AI hiring law kick in'. Covers US states, the EU, and the UK. Every date is quoted from the instrument itself — a signed bill, a session law, or the Official Journal — because the widely-repeated dates are frequently the superseded ones: Colorado's SB24-205 was moved to 2026-06-30 and then to 2027-01-01 by SB26-189, and the EU AI Act's Annex III high-risk date was moved from 2026-08-02 to 2027-12-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, while secondary trackers still print the old dates.
licence: Each record quotes one dating clause from an enacted bill, session law, or official journal and links to it. US federal and state statutes and the enrolled bills that make them are government edicts and are not subject to copyright (Banks v. Manchester; Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 2020). EU legislation published in the Official Journal is reusable under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU with source acknowledged. UK legislation on legislation.gov.uk is Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence v3.0. No instrument is reproduced in whole; what is taken is a fact plus a short attributed quote linking back.
